publicReleaseNotes:
Dial 0.5.1 supports hosted setup with mail off and owner sign-in through rer. It pins rer 0.2.140.

Deploy with `MAIL_PROVIDER=none` to set up hosted Dial without a mail sender or API key. The setup owner signs in with `rer signin`. Configure a mail provider before opening booking pages that send confirmations or management links.

This release also adds group seat capacity and English or Spanish booking confirmations. Archive preflight matches installed files against the rer migration ledger.

Back up Dial 0.5.0 before updating in place. Adopt 0.5.1 with the pinned rer 0.2.140 and apply the 39 pending migrations through the normal upgrade runner. Preserve the existing migration ledger and already applied SQL. Confirm owner access and check existing records before resuming writes.

screenshots.alt: Dial’s Bookings workspace showing confirmed, rescheduled and cancelled bookings, with host and invitee times.
screenshots.caption: The Bookings workspace shows the booking state and time for each participant.

contractChanges.EVENT-007: PARTIAL: native owner-session group capacity from 2 to 1,000 for free, unapproved single-host events with one fixed duration and location and no additional guests or connected calendar. Atomic seat admission, private per-invitee booking authority and reminders, individual cancellation, upgrade and archive custody are implemented. Controls, waitlist, whole-slot cancellation, shared calendar delivery and priced or approval group combinations remain unimplemented.
contractChanges.LOCALE-001: MISSING judgment retained pending clause review; added native proof: native owner-session English or Spanish confirmation language, defaulting existing events to English. Built-in invitee confirmations snapshot the language, keep operator text and named timezones, render Spanish dates with explicit 12-hour times, and freeze delivery bytes for retries. Ordinary edits, draft duplication and native archive restoration preserve configuration. Other languages, invitee surfaces, mail families, managed locale templates and browser qualification remain held.

Adds explicit delegated API consent, single-use PKCE authorization codes and native API host partitions. Existing machine applications keep client-credentials grants and existing credentials acquire no delegated grant. Recover with the pre-upgrade backup and matching code rather than resetting populated state.
